correctness.rationale: Deterministic upper bound and equality from squared vector sum; exact normalized three-Gram density and affine-slack transformation; independent cap-lens expansion with explicit spherical-geodesic second fundamental form and transverse ball integration fixes probability constant. Total mass independently equals the limiting gamma-simplex integral; Scheffe yields total-variation marked law even at the integrable d=3 Gram singularity. Direct simplex coordinate calculation gives independent Beta(3,(d-2)/2) and Dirichlet(1,1,1). A standalone conditional beta-integral numerical checker tested d=3,4,5 and gamma normalizations d=3,4,5,6,9. The analytic argument, not finite numerical tests, proves fixed-d asymptotics.

originality.rationale: The assertion is a sharply quantified first nontrivial spherical hard-cap packing boundary: exactly three uniform full-sphere points, minimum pairwise separation tends to 2pi/3 in fixed ambient dimension d>=3, gamma coefficient and total-variation slack shape law. The closest archival separation results have n->infinity and a small minimum angle; deterministic packing establishes only the optimum. A 2018 hard-cap canonical partition function definition does not supply this threshold law. Relevant public-record near-matches concern different random events (intrinsic triangle angles, perimeter, 4-point cap coverage). No checked publication implies the entire claimed coefficient and joint conditional law; historical uniqueness is provisional.
residual_risks: Older geometric-probability literature may contain a three-point threshold asymptotic under another normalization or as a special case of a general spherical packing-volume theorem.

value.rationale: Near-optimal volume of a three-particle spherical code is a natural hard-cap partition-function invariant, not a manufactured parameter choice. The optimum has rank-deficient planar Gram geometry with d-dependent tangency codimension; the exact positive coefficient and power (d+2)/2 quantify a meaningful threshold in every dimension. Conditional total-variation Beta(3,(d-2)/2) and uniform Dirichlet triplet split reveal how geometric constraints share the rare-event deficit. This is substantially more informative than the textbook deterministic 120-degree upper bound or a finite numerical enumeration.
